test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The leader applauded the comrades saying that they had done very well.

options.text: The leader said to the comrades, “Bravo! You have done very well.”
The leader said to the comrades, “Cheers! You have been doing very well.”
The leader said to the comrades, “Great! You could do very well.”
The leader said to the comrades, “Alas! You have done very well.”

solution:
The correct answer is "**The leader said to the comrades, “Bravo! You have done very well.”**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in indirect speech, which means it reports what the leader said without using his exact words.
 
• **To convert it into direct speech:**
 
 
• **We need to use the leader's exact words and add quotation marks**.
 
 
 
• The sentence structure changes to subject-verb-object, as we are reporting what the leader said directly to the comrades.
 
• The sentence ends with an exclamation mark to convey the leader's enthusiasm and appreciation for the comrades' performance.
 
 
• Thus the sentence is direct speech will be: The leader said to the comrades, “Bravo! You have done very well.”
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: The word "Cheers" is used to express good wishes or congratulations, but it is not as common as "Bravo" in this context.
 
• Option 3: The phrase "could do very well" implies a possibility or potential, but the original sentence is about an accomplishment that has already happened.
 
• Option 4: The word "Alas" is used to express sadness or regret, which is the opposite of the leader's positive feedback.
